clue.text: It shows you the way to follow " Yours truly"

parts.note: 'Yours truly' is the phrase written just before you sign a letter, so it stands for signing
post is Latin for after, as in postscript, the part that follows

explanation.surface: A pointer for someone looking for directions, signed off like a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is how a letter is signed off, so it points to signing; 'to follow' is the Latin prefix for 'after', as in postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer on a pole tells travellers which route to take.

clue.text: Put up with the evil and deputises

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate or put up with it
sin is wrongdoing, evil

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates wickedness while covering for a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to take another person's place for a while, a substitute's job.

clue.text: Ginger's managed to half suppress laugh

indicators.note: managed suggests handled or worked into shape, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is spelt out with its S, giving seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A red-haired person just about manages to stifle a giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges GINGERS, the name with its 's counted as a letter; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A snigger is a smothered, sly giggle, a laugh partly held back.

clue.text: A flying carrier of sickly sleep

definitions.text: A flying carrier of sickly sleep

parts.words: A flying carrier of sickly sleep
parts.note: describes the African biting fly that transmits sleeping sickness, with 'sickly sleep' turning the disease's name round

explanation.definitionFit: This African fly spreads trypanosomes, the parasites causing sleeping sickness in humans and cattle.

clue.text: Empty, gauge for a body travelling in space

annotationWithheld.why: 'Empty, gauge for a body travelling in space': the only parse is O (nothing) inside METER, with 'Empty' both supplying O and signalling the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Empty, gauge for a body travelling in space

clue.text: Dramatically moving picture

parts.note: looks like a touching film, but means the stage set changing during a play, a theatre picture that moves

explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, a set changed in view of the audience is a stage picture in motion.

clue.text: The knife-grinder's tricky business?

parts.note: a knife-grinder's trade is putting an edge on blades, while the phrase also means underhand dealing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for dishonest or unscrupulous dealing, and literally names the work of keeping blades keen.

clue.text: Washington campaigners are catching it!

parts.note: 'catching it' suggests an illness, here the excitement that grips American politicians before a vote

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the excitement and frenzy around a political vote, described as if it were an illness.

clue.text: Able to say "No" to French big shot?"

parts.note: to be able is 'can'
non is the French word for no

explanation.surface: A capable person refuses the French a powerful gunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A big gun fires heavy shot, so it is a 'big shot' read literally.

clue.text: Got an impression of bloodsucking type flying around there

indicators.note: the word for the insect goes around the word there, holding it inside

parts.note: gad is short for gadfly, a bloodsucking fly that bites cattle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone senses a horsefly buzzing about nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' describes the insect rather than signalling an anagram; the gadfly, a horsefly that bites livestock, is clipped to its first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer or understand, so having gathered something you have formed a view of it.

clue.text: Hound to hound

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a canine such as a hunting animal; as a verb it means to trail and pester someone.

clue.text: Golf clubs' spies making a come-back

indicators.note: coming back suggests going in the opposite direction, so the word for spies is read backwards

parts.note: snoops are people who pry, spies

explanation.surface: Agents at the golf club return to the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a come-back' turns SNOOPS round; the 's after 'clubs' is 'is' linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wooden golf clubs with lofted faces were called spoons, roughly equal to a modern three-wood.

clue.text: Something to send packing after Devon banker put a curse on it

indicators.note: after places the packing box behind the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river of Devon, England; a river has banks, so it is a 'banker'
a crate is a box goods are packed in to be sent

explanation.surface: Someone in Devon damns the box sent after a bank manager.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' is a river, something with banks; the Exe flows through Devon, a county in south-west England. 'it' is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or detest, to call down damnation on.

clue.text: Shy company an MP drops out of

indicators.note: dropping out means leaving, so these letters are taken out of the word company

parts.note: taken as written, Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician quits a firm because he is timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops out of' removes M, P, A, N from COMPANY, leaving C, O, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means bashful or reserved, unwilling to be forward.

clue.text: Indulge in play-acting in front of nurse

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before or in front of
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: An actor shows off before a hospital nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to make believe or act a part.

clue.text: An organ spike

definitions.meaning: the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant such as wheat

explanation.definitionFit: It is the body part we listen with, and also the seed head of corn.

clue.text: Don't be seen, but watch my lad nursing poor disheartened puppy.

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the son holds the rearranged puppy letters inside

parts.note: a son is a parent's lad

indicators.note: poor suggests out of shape, so the letters left are rearranged
losing its heart, the middle letter of the word puppy goes

explanation.surface: A parent tells a boy caring for a sad pup to keep watch unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle letter of PUPPY, and 'poor' rearranges the four letters left; the definition runs to 'watch', with 'but' part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy on someone is to watch them secretly without being noticed.

clue.text: Mere disturbance in head can become all-pervading

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of mere are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small upset in the mind can spread everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the definition's setting, but it gives the old word for the skull's top; 'disturbance' gives ERME, the anagram of MERE; 'can' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through or saturate every part of something.

clue.text: The lot nobody wanted apparently not asked to attend

definitions.meaning: an auction lot that received no bids, read as un-bid

explanation.definitionFit: At an auction an item no one bid for was not bid on; the word also means uninvited.

clue.text: Soft mixture Glamorgan turned up in one morning

indicators.note: in places the turned county letters within the other pieces

parts.note: A is one
AM stands for ante meridiem, morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Glam is the abbreviation for Glamorgan, a former Welsh county

explanation.surface: A Welsh county is churned into a gentle blend before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives MALG, GLAM read backwards, since in a down clue up means bottom to top. Glamorgan is a historic county in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend, and in particular a soft alloy of mercury used for tooth fillings.

clue.text: The glacial course echoes when I cry in terror

indicators.note: an echo repeats a sound, so the words before it are heard as another phrase

parts.note: a terrified person yells 'I scream'

explanation.surface: A frightened diner shrieks at a frozen dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'echoes' says the phrase 'I scream' sounds like the frozen dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This frozen sweet is served as the dessert, the icy course of a meal.

clue.text: Feeling crawly?

parts.note: a skin-crawling sensation of fear, and also the feeling of being like something that crawls

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a sinister, spine-tingling feeling, and literally means crawling.

clue.text: Seeing over the harem like Mardian in Cleopatra

definitions.text: Seeing over the harem like Mardian in Cleopatra

parts.words: Seeing over the harem like Mardian in Cleopatra
parts.note: Mardian is Cleopatra's castrated attendant in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra; such men guarded harems

explanation.definitionFit: Castrated men served as guardians of harems, and Shakespeare's Mardian is one such servant.

clue.text: Polish to brush up or check?

definitions.meaning: to buff again, polish once more
to snub or repulse, check an advance

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-buff it means shine up again; as one word it means repel or refuse bluntly.

clue.text: I am about to prepare to fire

indicators.note: about suggests turning around, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gunner announces they are on the point of shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the three letters of I AM; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Before shooting you level the weapon at the target, sighting it.

clue.text: Seasonal description of the rest of the hedgehogs

definitions.text: Seasonal description of the rest of the hedgehogs

parts.words: Seasonal description of the rest of the hedgehogs
parts.note: hedgehogs rest through the cold months, so the adjective for that season describes their sleep

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of winter, the season when hedgehogs sleep through the cold.

clue.text: Strangely veined growth in the salad bowl

indicators.note: strangely suggests oddly arranged, so the letters of veined are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leaf with odd veins turns up among the lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: This bitter leafy plant, a chicory relative, is grown for salads.

clue.text: Next in line, waiting to come into the stately home?

definitions.text: Next in line, waiting to come into the stately home?

parts.words: Next in line, waiting to come into the stately home?
parts.note: an heir waiting to inherit a country house, with 'come into' meaning both enter and inherit

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a successor who will inherit, here a grand house on the death of its owner.
